# shader_53 — 3×3 convolution over two 4-channel inputs + bias + additive skip

## 1. Interface

- **Workgroup size**: 16 × 16 × 1 (`LocalSize 16 16 1`).
- Uses `gl_GlobalInvocationID` only. One thread = one output texel:
  `p = ivec2(gl_GlobalInvocationID.xy)`.
- Requires fp16 arithmetic (`Float16` capability). All matrix products and
  accumulation are IEEE fp16.
- No UBO, no push constants, no spec constants, no shared memory.

Descriptors (all descriptor set 0):

| binding | kind | format | access | role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | combined image sampler, 2D float | — | read | input **X** (4 channels), sampled at 9 taps of a 3×3 neighborhood; its size defines the UV normalization |
| 33 | combined image sampler, 2D float | — | read | input **Y** (4 channels), sampled at the same 9 taps |
| 34 | combined image sampler, 2D float | — | read | skip input **K** (4 channels), sampled once at center, added verbatim |
| 48 | storage image 2D | `Rgba16f` | write-only (`NonReadable`) | output |

## 2. Coordinates and early-out

```
ivec2 p = ivec2(gl_GlobalInvocationID.xy);
if (p.x >= imageSize(out).x || p.y >= imageSize(out).y) return;   // signed compare
vec2 uv = (vec2(p) + 0.5) / vec2(textureSize(sampler_binding32, 0));
```

All samples use this single `uv`, LOD 0. Taps use GLSL
`textureLodOffset(tex, uv, 0.0, o)` — the offset is in texels of the sampled
texture. The shader does no coordinate clamping of its own; border taps
resolve per the externally-configured sampler address mode. Only the upper
bound of the output size is guarded (`p` is never negative).

## 3. Behavior

Let `x(o) = f16vec4(textureLodOffset(tex32, uv, 0.0, o))` and
`y(o) = f16vec4(textureLodOffset(tex33, uv, 0.0, o))` (the `(0,0)` tap is a
plain `textureLod`), and `k = f16vec4(textureLod(tex34, uv, 0.0))`.

`M · v` is the standard column-matrix product
`M.col0*v.x + M.col1*v.y + M.col2*v.z + M.col3*v.w` (GLSL `f16mat4 * f16vec4`
with columns as listed in §4).

The output value is accumulated in exactly this order (18 fp16 mat4·vec4
products, summed left-to-right; then bias; then skip):

```
acc =  MX[1]·x(-1,-1) + MX[2]·x(-1,0) + MX[3]·x(-1,+1)
     + MX[4]·x( 0,-1) + MX[5]·x( 0,0) + MX[6]·x( 0,+1)
     + MX[7]·x(+1,-1) + MX[8]·x(+1,0) + MX[9]·x(+1,+1)
     + MY[1]·y(-1,-1) + MY[2]·y(-1,0) + MY[3]·y(-1,+1)
     + MY[4]·y( 0,-1) + MY[5]·y( 0,0) + MY[6]·y( 0,+1)
     + MY[7]·y(+1,-1) + MY[8]·y(+1,0) + MY[9]·y(+1,+1)
acc = acc + BIAS
acc = acc + k
imageStore(out, p, vec4(acc))        // f16 -> f32 convert; Rgba16f target
```

Offsets are `(ox, oy)`, +x right, +y down. No clamp anywhere; Rgba16f
preserves the fp16 values exactly.

Interpretation (not normative): a 3×3 convolution layer with 8 input
channels (two RGBA textures) and 4 output channels, plus bias, plus an
elementwise residual/skip connection from a third texture.

## 4. Weights (exact fp16 decimals; matrices as 4 columns)

Tap index order: 1..9 = (-1,-1), (-1,0), (-1,+1), (0,-1), (0,0), (0,+1),
(+1,-1), (+1,0), (+1,+1).

## 5. Control flow summary

Straight-line: one early-out bounds check, 19 texture samples, 18 fp16
matrix-vector products accumulated in the order of §3, bias, skip add, one
store. No loops.
